fn.en: Talk about your family and say who people and things belong to.

lines: Your mother’s sister is your [aunt|uncle|niece]. Her son is your [cousin|nephew|brother].
Two children born on the same day to the same mother are [twins|cousins|parents].

sub.en: Look at the examples. Where does the apostrophe go when the owner is plural?

items.why: One owner → ’s.  More than one owner → s’.
With two names, only the second one takes ’s.
his = belonging to him.  he’s = he is.

items.q: The dog is old. ___ name is Rex.
items.why: its = belonging to it.  it’s = it is.

items.q: My two ___ children live in Poland. (one uncle)

rows: The dog’s name is Rex. Its name is Rex.

acts.title: Zafar’s family
text: Zafar is a doctor and his wife, Amina, is a teacher. They have two sons: Hasan and his twin brother, Tariq.
Hasan is single and lives in Manchester. Tariq is married to Rafina. Their daughter, Sahala, is three years old — so Sahala is Zafar and Amina’s granddaughter.
Amina’s sister, Nadia, lives next door. Nadia is Hasan and Tariq’s aunt, and her son Bilal is their cousin.
Nadia is divorced. Her ex-husband’s family still comes to every birthday, because in this family nobody stops being family.

items.q: The word for your aunt’s son.
The word for the daughter of your son or daughter.
The word for your mother’s sister.
The adjective for somebody whose marriage has ended.

tts: I’m his son. — He’s my father.
Is he your brother? — You’re right.
She’s our teacher. — Are you married?

It’s my ___ flat. She lives on the fourth floor. 🏠

write.q: Describe your family: 6 sentences. Name five people and say who they are. Use my, his, her and their, and at least two possessive ’s or s’.
write.model: This is my family. My parents live in Karaganda and my mother’s sister lives next door. Her son Bilal is my cousin — we were at school together. My brother is married; his wife is a teacher. Their daughter is three, so she’s my niece. The house on the corner is my grandparents’ house.

speak.q: Answer out loud: Who is your mother’s sister to you? Who is your sister’s daughter? Are you married or single? Then describe two people in your family.
speak.model: My mother’s sister is my aunt. My sister’s daughter is my niece. I’m single. My brother is married and his wife is a doctor — their son is my nephew.
